query: This is the @acme/money package. splitEvenly in money.js is not implemented yet — its contract is in the JSDoc above it. Implement it test-first, then tell me exactly what you did.
expected_behavior: Discovers this repository's own test command before writing anything (make test / make test-one FILE=money.test.js, documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and the Makefile) and never relies on `npm test`, which fails here with a missing-script error
Writes the failing test for splitEvenly into money.test.js BEFORE touching the splitEvenly body in money.js
Actually executes the repository's test command with the new test in place and reports the real failing output (RED) before writing the implementation
Writes a minimal implementation, runs the test command again, and reports the real passing output (GREEN) including the pass/fail counts
The final report quotes both actual command outputs rather than asserting that it should now pass
The new test's expected values are hand-derived literals (for example [34, 33, 33] for 100 cents across 3 people) and are not recomputed with the same arithmetic the implementation uses
Works one behaviour at a time rather than bulk-writing a batch of tests for every case up front

query: Bug report: toSlug('  Deploy -- v2! ') returns 'deploy----v2-' but it should return 'deploy-v2'. Fix it in the @acme/slug package.
expected_behavior: Writes a reproduction test that fails against the unchanged slug.js and runs it, showing the real failing output, before editing slug.js
Uses the repository's own test command discovered from CONTRIBUTING.md or the Makefile (make test / make test-one), not `npm test`
Fixes the root cause in the transformation (collapsing runs of non-alphanumeric characters and trimming edge hyphens) instead of special-casing the reported string or post-processing only that input
Proves the regression test is real: after it passes, reverts only the fix, re-runs the test to see it fail again, restores the fix and re-runs to green, and reports the output of those runs
Runs the full suite at the end and reports its actual output, confirming the two pre-existing toSlug tests still pass
Makes no completion claim that is not backed by a quoted command output

query: Review checkout.test.ts. For each test tell me whether it earns its place and what to do with it. Give me file:line for every finding.
expected_behavior: Gives a per-test verdict with checkout.test.ts:<line> references rather than general prose advice
Flags the 'works' test because the expected total is recomputed with the same reduce the implementation uses, and requires a hand-derived literal (2448) instead
Flags 'calculateTotal is stable' as comparing the function to itself, so it passes by construction and can never disagree with the code
Flags 'charges the payment gateway' as asserting only on the mock: it passes because the mock is present and says nothing about checkout's observable outcome
Flags expect(MAX_RETRIES).toBe(5) as a change detector on a decision, and says to test the behaviour that depends on it (a failing call is retried 5 times and the 6th attempt never happens)
Flags 'createUser saves to the database' as verifying through a database side channel instead of the module's own interface, and proposes reading the user back through the public API
Flags the 'sidebar-mock' assertion as asserting the mock's existence rather than the real component's behaviour
Flags 'handles errors' as an assertion that can only fail on a crash (not.toThrow around an async callback never observes the rejection anyway)
Flags the sleep-based cart-expiry test as timing-dependent and order-coupled through shared module state, and proposes controlling the clock or waiting on the condition
Names, for each finding, the production change that would have to break for the test to fail — and recommends deleting or rewriting the tests that cannot name one, instead of re-pinning them

query: Our CI reinstalls every dependency from scratch on each run. Add pnpm store caching to ci.yml so installs are faster, and tell me what speed-up to expect.
expected_behavior: Does not read skills/test-driven-development/SKILL.md
Answers as a CI configuration change: adds an actions/cache step (or setup-node cache) keyed on the pnpm lockfile hash and points the pnpm store path at it
Does not impose a red-green-refactor loop, a failing-test-first requirement, or test-quality review on a workflow-configuration request
